chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The pure period (tuhr) cannot be less than ten days; and whatever exceeds that — the minimum of it is ten, from the time she becomes pure until she sees the blood.

key_terms.أَقَلَّ مِنْ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: Less than ten days — the minimum threshold that defines a valid tuhr
key_terms.الدَّمَ: The blood — refers to the onset of the next menstrual cycle
key_terms.الْقُرْءُ: The tuhr (pure period between menstrual cycles); used here specifically for the intermenstrual interval
key_terms.تَطْهُرُ: She becomes pure — the moment haydh ends and tuhr begins

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum length of the tuhr (pure period) between menstrual cycles according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a legal ruling that the minimum tuhr (period of purity between two menstrual cycles) is ten days. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining whether bleeding qualifies as haydh (menstruation) or istihadha (dysfunctional uterine bleeding). The original audience of Shia jurists would have understood this as a binding ruling by the Imam, whose pronouncements on fiqh carry the authority of divine guidance.
